import html # Predefined HTML template for the invitation. INVITATION_FORMAT = """ {event_title}

{event_title}

{event_description}

Date: {event_date}

{additional_notes}
""" def _sanitize_html(text: str) -> str: """ Escape special HTML characters and preserve line breaks by converting newline sequences into
tags. This mitigates XSS and ensures the output is well‑formed HTML. """ # Escape HTML special characters first escaped = html.escape(text, quote=True) # Convert line breaks to
tags return escaped.replace("\n", "
") def create_event_invitation( title: str, description: str, date: str, notes: str ) -> str: """ Generate a secure, sanitized HTML invitation for an event. Parameters ---------- title : str The event's title or name. description : str A comprehensive description of the event. May contain multiple paragraphs and formatting. date : str The scheduled date of the event. notes : str Any supplementary information or instructions provided by the organizer. Returns ------- str A sanitized HTML string ready for safe rendering in a browser. Raises ------ ValueError If any required argument is missing or not a string. """ # Basic type checks for arg_name, arg_value in ( ("title", title), ("description", description), ("date", date), ("notes", notes) ): if not isinstance(arg_value, str): raise ValueError(f"{arg_name!r} must be a string") # Sanitize each field safe_title = _sanitize_html(title) safe_description = _sanitize_html(description) safe_date = _sanitize_html(date) safe_notes = _sanitize_html(notes) # Format the final HTML invitation_html = INVITATION_FORMAT.format( event_title=safe_title, event_description=safe_description, event_date=safe_date, additional_notes=safe_notes ) return invitation_html.strip()
